blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes Over $1.8M Topic: streets and boundaries

items.t: This band has no streets of its own: it is a price filter applied across the whole City of Maple Ridge, not a neighbourhood, plan area or board designation, so the boundary a buyer checks is the municipal boundary and the parcel's own zone, not a band boundary.

The City's own neighbourhood list names the east-side areas where this band's rural and acreage stock sits: Webster's Corners, Whonnock, Ruskin, Thornhill and Silver Valley, alongside Albion/Kanaka, Port Hammond, Port Haney, Town Centre and Yennadon.
Webster's Corners sits near the border of Maple Ridge and Mission, just off Dewdney Trunk Road, according to the City's neighbourhood page.
Ruskin is described by the City as an area along the Stave River, and Silver Valley as located on the north side of the Alouette River.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes Over $1.8M Topic: the housing stock

items.t: Above this band the stock is defined less by house style than by land: the rural zones in Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 set subdivision minimums far above urban lots — A-1 (Small Holding Agricultural, s.501) 2.0 hectares, A-2 (Upland Agricultural, s.502) 4.0 hectares and A-3 (Extensive Agricultural, s.503) 8.0 hectares, each with the lot width and depth set out in Schedule B of the bylaw.

The two rural residential zones sit below the agricultural zones in lot size: RS-2 (Single Detached Suburban Residential, s.610) has a subdivision minimum of 0.4 hectares, and RS-3 (Single Detached Rural Residential, s.611) has a minimum of 0.8 hectares where a community water system is available and 2.0 hectares where it is not, per Schedule B and s.611.4 of the same bylaw.

In the A-1 and A-3 zones, single detached residential use is limited to one dwelling per lot, and buildings for that use are capped at 10% lot coverage under ss.501.5–501.6 and 503.5–503.6 of the bylaw.
Thornhill, one of the east-side areas this band reaches, is described by the City as a heavily forested, mainly residential area with several farms and nurseries.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes Over $1.8M Topic: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Agricultural zoning carries its own residential limits: in the A-1, A-2 and A-3 zones the permitted principal uses are Agricultural, Cannabis Commercial Production, Forest Resource and Single Detached Residential, as ss.501.2, 502.2 and 503.2 of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 state them.
On a lot inside the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR), the City's Farm Home Plate requirements in s.402 of the zoning bylaw apply, as s.501.11 of the bylaw states for A-1 lots.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes Over $1.8M Topic: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Thornhill has a mountain biking and hiking trail network on 256 Street, which the City counts at 17 trails, described as moderately difficult and typically taking an hour to complete.
Ruskin still has a number of shake and sawmills active along the Stave River, and the Ruskin Community Hall remains a meeting place for the local community, according to the City.
Whonnock Lake Park, in the Whonnock neighbourhood, has a small sandy beach, a swimming area and hiking trails, and the Ridge Canoe and Kayak Club is based on Whonnock Lake.
Webster's Corners holds the BCIT Woodlot trail network used by mountain bikers, and the City also names the area as an active hub for film production in Maple Ridge.

Kanaka Creek Regional Park, on the Albion side of the city, holds the Bell-Irving Hatchery and fish fence, which Metro Vancouver states support salmonid enhancement for chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout in Kanaka Creek.

In the ALR, a secondary suite is permitted only when it is entirely contained within the principal residence; a separate or detached dwelling cannot be used as the suite, under the ALC's housing rules.

Replacing a house on ALR land has a sequencing rule: the ALC states a new principal residence may be built without an application if the existing one is demolished and removed first, but ALC approval is required to keep living in the existing residence while the new one is constructed.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes Over $1.8M Topic: development and new projects

items.t: Full entry for this page: the Silver Valley Area Plan update was adopted on November 25, 2025; the City states the update modernizes the 2002 plan, consolidates and updates land use designations and policies, adds a zoning matrix, and incorporates additional density as required by provincial legislation — the plan layer a buyer checks for parcels in Silver Valley, an area this band reaches.
The City's December 4, 2025 release adds that the Silver Valley update introduces a River Village Mixed-Use designation to encourage development of a complete community.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes Over $1.8M Topic: costs and taxes

items.t: Property Transfer Tax (PTT) is the cost that changes shape in this band: the Province states the general rate is 1% of fair market value up to and including $200,000, 2% of the portion greater than $200,000 and up to and including $2,000,000, and 3% of the portion greater than $2,000,000.

Above $3,000,000 a further tax applies: the Province states that if a property has residential property worth over $3,000,000, a further 2% tax is applied to the residential property value greater than $3,000,000.

On a mixed-class property that further 2% applies only to the residential portion, and where land is classed as farm only because it is used for an owner's or farmer's dwelling, up to 0.5 hectares is treated as residential property — a point that bears directly on farm-classed acreages in this band.

PTT is calculated on the fair market value of the property, meaning land and improvements, on the day it is registered at the Land Title Office, and the Province states it is not the same as annual property taxes.

A foreign national, foreign corporation or taxable trustee must also pay the additional property transfer tax on the fair market value of the residential portion of a property within a specified area of British Columbia, as the Province's PTT page states.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes Over $1.8M Topic: getting around

items.t: For the east-side areas this band reaches, road position is the practical check: the City places Webster's Corners just off Dewdney Trunk Road near the Mission border, which is the corridor a buyer there uses toward both city centres.

Kanaka Creek Regional Park's trails are a local on-foot and on-bike link on the Albion side: Metro Vancouver states the Canyon Trail runs 1.2 kilometres one way from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls, and the Riverfront Trails run 3 kilometres one way.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes Over $1.8M Topic: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check ALR status parcel by parcel before anything else on a rural purchase: the ALC directs buyers to its maps and online mapping tools to answer whether a property is in the ALR, and no area-wide statement substitutes for that parcel check.

Check what the ALR status does to the building plan: a residence larger than the ALC's permitted size, or more residences than permitted, requires ALC approval, and the Commission states approval for an additional residence beyond what is permitted can only be given where the residence is necessary for farm use.

Check fill before planning construction on ALR land: the ALC lists a Notice of Intent to place fill among the approvals that may be required, alongside local government zoning and building permits and health authority approval for septic systems.

Check servicing on RS-3 land specifically: the zoning bylaw states that zone may not be connected to the community water system or the community sanitary sewer system, so well and septic condition are parcel-level checks, not assumptions.

Check creek-adjacent parcels against the watercourse itself: Metro Vancouver states Kanaka Creek provides habitat for a variety of wildlife including salmon, and that steep, slippery cliffs occur in many places along the creek, especially at Cliff Falls.

faq.a: The cards visible in the page text are labelled Albion, Silver Valley, Thornhill and Southwest Maple Ridge. The detached inventory evidence shows the deepest pools in East Central (82), West Central (66), Albion (62), Cottonwood (55) and Silver Valley (49), and thin rural pools in Thornhill (13), Websters Corners (8), Northeast (2) and Whonnock (2) — inventory counts only, not price evidence for any sub-area (SnapStats, September 2026)
faq.q: Which Maple Ridge areas carry the homes on this page?

faq.a: Three, all parcel-specific: ALR status, through the Agricultural Land Commission's maps and online mapping tools; floodplain status on Fraser River frontage (flood construction level 6.7 m geodetic, covenant on title); and escarpment status on the south-western slopes (geotechnical report within 300 m of the crest).
faq.q: What parcel checks matter most on a Maple Ridge acreage over $1.8M?

faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.
faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Maple Ridge?

faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.
